summary: Design reporting lineage, validation controls, and supervisory calendars. Explore the practical course and its applied curriculum.
lede: Banking and insurance reporting training helps reporting teams trace supervisory returns from source data through to submission. For reporting managers, controllers, analysts and data-governance specialists, it covers building reporting inventories and lineage records, designing data-quality and validation controls, and organizing review and reporting calendars. Using BCBS 239 and XBRL concepts as reference points, participants also explore taxonomy governance, insurer-data reconciliations and conceptual AI-assisted exception triage.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who prepare, govern, validate, review, or supervise bank and insurance regulatory returns. This course is designed for: Bank Regulatory Reporting Managers coordinating prudential return preparation and sign-off. Insurance Regulatory Reporting Managers reconciling policy and claims data to supervisory returns. Finance Controllers reviewing regulatory figures against ledger and close processes. Regulatory Reporting Analysts tracing source data and resolving submission exceptions. Risk Data Governance Leads assigning ownership for risk reporting elements. Compliance Officers mapping supervisory instructions to reporting controls and evidence. Financial Data Architects documenting system-to-return lineage and transformation logic. Internal Auditors testing regulatory reporting controls and retained review evidence. Insurance Actuaries validating reported policy, claims, and liability data. Financial Supervisors assessing reporting completeness, consistency, and data quality.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with bank, insurer, pension, or other financial-sector reporting processes is recommended. No coding is required. You may bring an anonymized reporting workflow or return example for contextual exercises; do not use confidential or identifiable data.
